en: Mayon Volcano in Albay features a nearly perfect symmetrical cone shape that is easily visible from many miles away.
The Puerto Princesa Subterranean River in Palawan flows directly into the sea, making its lower water levels affected by ocean tides.
Taal Lake in Batangas contains Volcano Island, which itself holds a smaller body of water called Main Crater Lake.
Mount Apo in Davao is the highest Philippine peak and features mossy forests alongside visible geothermal steam vents.
The giant Rafflesia flower found in Philippine rainforests blooms on the forest floor with a distinct rotting meat odor.
The grass-covered mounds of the Chocolate Hills in Bohol turn brown during the dry season, resembling giant chocolate pieces.
During the amihan season, the Philippines experiences cool northeast monsoon winds that bring dry and pleasant weather to most areas.
The white sand beaches of Boracay in Aklan are primarily composed of finely crushed coral reefs and shells.
Pagsanjan Falls in Laguna is hidden between two steep, narrow river gorges covered in lush tropical vegetation.
Callao Cave in Peñablanca, Cagayan, features a natural rock chapel illuminated by sunlight streaming through an opening in the ceiling.
Mangrove forests in coastal provinces like Pangasinan have specialized stilt roots that visibly rise above the muddy tidal water.
The Banaue Rice Terraces in Ifugao are carved into steep mountain slopes, creating giant stairways that follow the natural contours.
